# Model Comparison and Robustness

- [Predictive comparison and model uncertainty](#predictive-comparison-and-model-uncertainty)
- [Robustness and defensible conclusions](#robustness-and-defensible-conclusions)

## Predictive comparison and model uncertainty

- Bayes factors, predictive assessment, and prior sensitivity
- Model averaging and uncertainty after selecting a model

Agresti 7.1

## Robustness and defensible conclusions

- Sensitivity to likelihoods and priors; robust alternatives
- Compare what the model learns with what the data can identify

Agresti 7.2; BDA and Efron–Hastie references

# Selected Extensions

- [Mixtures and multivariate models](#mixtures-and-multivariate-models)
- [Choose breadth deliberately](#choose-breadth-deliberately)

## Mixtures and multivariate models

- A small finite-mixture model and label switching
- Selected multivariate-response or covariance modeling

Supplements retain advanced topics from the old syllabus

## Choose breadth deliberately

- Select among classification, missing data, or network examples
- A Gaussian-process illustration is optional and displaces another extension

Selected Agresti 7.3–7.5; Reich–Ghosh or BDA supplements

# Synthesis and Communication

- [Follow one analysis from question to conclusion](#follow-one-analysis-from-question-to-conclusion)
- [Planned Python demonstration](#planned-python-demonstration)

## Follow one analysis from question to conclusion

- Model, prior, computation, diagnostics, prediction, and sensitivity
- Communicate uncertainty and limitations in a real-data study

Integrative discussion within this unit's hour budget

## Planned Python demonstration

- Compare two defensible models and explain their predictive differences
- Select optional extensions only after core Bayesian objectives are secure

No companion notebook released yet
